title: Repair Windows with the built-in recovery tools
description: Use Windows Recovery Environment, Safe Mode, System File Checker, DISM and Reset this PC to fix a Windows installation that will not start or behaves badly.
objectives: Choose the right repair tool for the symptom, least destructive first.
Repair system files with DISM and SFC.
Know what Reset this PC keeps and removes.
tools: Windows installation USB (if WinRE does not start)

safety.text: Back up the customer's files before Reset this PC or any option that can remove data.
Use the least destructive repair first. Resetting or reinstalling should be the last resort.

steps.title: Open the recovery environment
steps.body:
Any of these opens **WinRE**:

- Hold **Shift** while clicking **Restart**.
- **Settings → System → Recovery → Advanced startup → Restart now**.
- Windows opens it automatically after startup fails twice in a row.
- Boot from a Windows installation USB and choose **Repair your computer**.

Then go to **Troubleshoot → Advanced options**.

steps.title: Try Startup Repair and System Restore
steps.body:
- **Startup Repair** fixes common problems that stop Windows from loading.
- **System Restore** returns system files and settings to an earlier restore point. It does not remove personal files, but programs installed after that point are removed.
- **Uninstall Updates** removes the latest quality or feature update if a bad update caused the fault.

steps.title: Use Safe Mode
steps.body:
**Safe Mode** starts Windows with only essential drivers. Use it to remove a bad driver or program, or to scan for malware.

In WinRE: **Troubleshoot → Advanced options → Startup Settings → Restart**, then press **4** (Safe Mode) or **5** (Safe Mode with Networking).

steps.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
steps.body:
Open **Command Prompt as administrator** and run:

```
DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth
```

This repairs the Windows component store that SFC uses. Then run:

```
sfc /scannow
```

This checks protected system files and replaces damaged ones. Restart when they finish.

steps.title: Check the disk and the memory
steps.body:
- `chkdsk C: /f` checks the file system and fixes errors. On the system drive it runs at the next restart.
- **Windows Memory Diagnostic** (`mdsched.exe`) tests the RAM at restart. Memory errors cause crashes that no software repair can fix.

steps.title: Reset this PC (last resort)
steps.body:
**Settings → System → Recovery → Reset PC**, or in WinRE **Troubleshoot → Reset this PC**:

- **Keep my files** reinstalls Windows but keeps personal files. Installed programs and settings are removed.
- **Remove everything** erases files, programs and settings.

Back up first, even when choosing Keep my files.

expectedResults: You can open WinRE in more than one way.
You choose repairs from least to most destructive.
Windows starts normally and SFC reports no remaining integrity violations.

commonMistakes.mistake: Going straight to Reset this PC.
commonMistakes.why: It removes programs and settings, and the problem may have had a much simpler fix.
commonMistakes.fix: Try Startup Repair, System Restore, Safe Mode and SFC/DISM first.

commonMistakes.mistake: Running SFC in a normal Command Prompt.
commonMistakes.why: SFC needs administrator rights and reports an error without them.
commonMistakes.fix: Right-click Command Prompt or Terminal and choose Run as administrator.

commonMistakes.why: Failing RAM or a failing drive causes repeated corruption that software repairs cannot fix.
commonMistakes.fix: Run Memory Diagnostic and check the drive's health (S.M.A.R.T.).

knowledgeChecks.question: What does System Restore remove?
knowledgeChecks.answer: Programs, drivers and updates installed after the restore point. It keeps personal files.

knowledgeChecks.question: In which order do you run DISM and SFC?
What is the difference between the two Reset this PC options?
knowledgeChecks.answer: Keep my files keeps personal files but removes programs and settings; Remove everything erases all of it.
